title.value: Annotation Cost-Sensitive Deep Active Learning with Limited Data (Student Abstract)
title.justification: The title of the paper is directly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: Annotation Cost-Sensitive Deep Active Learning with Limited Data (Student Abstract)

extractions.description: This paper explores a deep learning approach to active learning in the context of biomedical imaging, where the cost of annotation is significant. It focuses on reducing the labeling cost by considering and learning annotation costs during active learning. The study leverages a classification task using the MNIST dataset to simulate the process and proposes methods to balance the annotation cost and model accuracy.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on the development of deep learning methodologies for active learning in biomedical imaging without an explicit emphasis on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Deep learning is a promising avenue to automate tedious analysis tasks in biomedical imaging.

primary_category.justification: The main focus of the paper is on the technical development of active learning and cost reduction in biomedical imaging, which does not align with any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category.
primary_category.quote: In this work, we show how annotation cost can be considered by AL agents and how it can be learned during the AL process.

secondary_categories.justification: Secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development are not present in the paper, as it is focused on machine learning techniques in biomedical contexts.
secondary_categories.quote: While these preliminary results are limited to the synthetic task crafted from the MNIST dataset, we plan on deploying these methods on a real-world problem in biophotonics.

primary_sub_category.justification: There is no specific sub-category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development addressed in this paper, as it primarily discusses machine learning and annotation costs in biomedical imaging.
primary_sub_category.quote: We simulate the annotation cost of an image using two components: i) a base acquisition cost that depends on the MNIST class, and ii) an annotation cost calculated from the perimeter of the binarized digit within each image.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not cover specific sub-categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development since its focus lies in reducing annotation costs for machine learning applications in biomedicine.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The training of supervised deep learning models requires vast amount of labeled training data.

applications.justification: The applications discussed in the paper pertain to the field of biomedical imaging and do not have a direct connection to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
applications.quote: Ultimately, we hope that such AL approaches will increase the accessibility of deep learning-based analysis to generate adequate datasets in application fields where annotation and acquisition costs are not negligible.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new category relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development; it focuses on machine learning in biomedical contexts.
new_primary_category.quote: Active learning (AL) aims to alleviate this issue by reducing the required quantity of data to label by selecting the most informative sample within an unlabeled dataset.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The document does not propose new sub-categories relevant to sustainable development, as it is heavily focused on methodological improvements in active learning for biomedical applications.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We next conduct experiments which consider the annotation cost in the image selection phase.
